definition: σαλεύω (σάλος), [in LXX for מוֹט, זוּעַ, etc. ;] prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mat.11:7, Luk.7:24; a house, Luk.6:48, Act.4:31 16:26; the earth, Heb.12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:25, Luk.21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Luk.6:38. Metaphorical,  __(a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., Heb.12:27;  __(b) with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security and happiness:  Act.2:25 (LXX);  __(with) to unsettle or drive away: pass., before ἀπὸ τ. νοός, 2Th.2:2;  __(d) to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, Act.17:13.† (AS)
